title: 🔗 Discourse Markers

sections.heading: What they do
sections.body:
Discourse markers are words and phrases that organise your writing and signal the relationship between ideas. They are essential for Coherence & Cohesion (25% of your Writing score).

They help the reader follow your argument by showing:
• When you're adding information
• When you're contrasting ideas
• When you're drawing a conclusion
• When you're giving an example

sections.heading: Categories
sections.body:
➕ Adding: Furthermore, Moreover, In addition, Additionally, Not only...but also

↔️ Contrasting: However, Nevertheless, On the other hand, Conversely, Despite this, Notwithstanding

➡️ Result: Consequently, Therefore, As a result, Hence, Thus

💡 Example: For instance, For example, To illustrate, A case in point, Specifically

🔚 Concluding: In conclusion, To summarise, Overall, In sum, Ultimately

highlight: DO NOT overuse discourse markers. Band 6 essays start every sentence with "Furthermore" or "However". Band 9 essays vary their cohesive devices and sometimes embed them mid-sentence.

example.wrong: Furthermore, technology is useful. Furthermore, it helps students. Furthermore, it saves time. However, it has problems. However, these can be managed.
example.right: Technology offers considerable educational benefits; however, its unrestricted use presents genuine risks that educators must thoughtfully manage.

question: Which discourse marker shows RESULT or CONSEQUENCE?
explanation:
"Consequently" introduces the result of what was previously stated.

Furthermore/Moreover = add more information
Nevertheless = contrast (something is true despite difficulty)

Result markers: Consequently, Therefore, Hence, Thus, As a result, For this reason

Example: "Air quality has deteriorated significantly. Consequently, respiratory diseases have become more prevalent."
hint: Think: "as a result of what was just said..." Which word fits?

sentence: Urban farming requires significant investment. _______, the long-term environmental benefits may well outweigh the initial costs.
explanation:
"Nevertheless" acknowledges the problem (high cost) while maintaining the argument (benefits are still worth it).

It means: "even though this is true, the main point still stands."

"Therefore" would suggest the investment LEADS to the benefits being worth it — illogical here
"Furthermore" just adds more — doesn't create the contrast needed
hint: The sentence first raises a problem, then argues the benefits still win — that's a concession+contrast.

explanation: "Notwithstanding" and "Accordingly" are Band 8+ formal alternatives to "Despite" and "Therefore". Using them appropriately impresses examiners.

title: Discourse Marker Error
instruction: Find the incorrectly used discourse marker:

sentences.text: The population is ageing rapidly. Consequently, healthcare costs are rising.
Technology has many benefits. Despite this, it has some advantages too.
sentences.explanation:
"Despite this" signals CONTRAST — it introduces something that goes AGAINST the previous point.

But "it has advantages" AGREES with "technology has benefits" — you can't contrast them.

✅ Correct: "Technology has many benefits. Furthermore/Moreover, it has some advantages too."
✅ Or: "Technology has many drawbacks. Despite this, it remains widely adopted."

sentences.text: Social media has increased connectivity. Nevertheless, feelings of isolation persist.
